analysis: The PR is documentation and changelog only, so no code paths changed. Three themes in the docs matter for security. (1) attestation.md defers to the Layr-Labs/darkbloom-platform contract, pinned at commit 20b8216. That contract separates EvaluateAuthorization from EvaluateReceiptMonitoring. Missing recurring receipt or risk evidence no longer blocks basic serving, and an established identity may retain last-known policy on failed admin reads, bounded by the original proof and admin ceilings (reported, attestation.md head line 112). The canonical threat model (T-053/T-055/T-057/TB-011) is not updated, although a changelog line claims alignment. (2) The new protocol-1 endpoint-custody resume responder in CoordinatorClient (provider.md head lines 66-77, attestation.md head lines 69-76) is a new proof message with no threat entry (reported, head line 69). The docs say it does no Apple work, creates no local authorization, and uses a per-socket nonce. (3) The changelog says logout now drains the provider and revokes the token against the running coordinator. It also says the resume control-frame limit is checked before decoding, and that UTF-16/32 JSON is rejected. These fixes live in code outside this batch, so their correctness is unverified here. The next pass should check the Swift responder, the logout revocation URL handling, and the platform repo's actual receipt, admin-read-failure and revocation behavior.

findings.detail: The rewritten Context paragraph says a platform revision's basic serving no longer depends on recurring receipt or risk evidence. It also allows an established identity to retain last-known policy when administrative reads fail, up to the 'original proof and administrative ceilings'. The base text and the canonical threat model assume the opposite. The base attestation.md required a verified current risk receipt with a complete metric for every grant. T-053 and T-055 assume revocation and policy changes are read live, and T-057 assumes grants fail when evidence is missing. A revocation or qualification change made during an administrative-read outage could therefore be honored late. A provider with a lapsed receipt or risk metric could also keep serving. The PR changes no threat-model file even though its changelog claims to keep the retained threat model aligned. The paragraph also leaves this repo's coordinator snapshot and the linked platform contract (pinned to an external commit) describing different grant rules. Update T-053, T-055, T-057 and TB-011 to record the new ceilings, and state which implementation is authoritative.
findings.title: Docs adopt weaker serving-authorization semantics while the threat model still assumes receipt-required grants

findings.detail: The PR adds a protocol-1 endpoint-custody response. CoordinatorClient answers it synchronously, using the in-memory X25519 key and a fresh nonce per socket. A platform implementation can use the response to resume authorization with retained evidence across same-process reconnects. This adds a new proof-of-key-custody message on TB-002/TB-011. Its replay resistance, nonce and origin binding, and the rule that retained evidence may not extend proof deadlines are asserted only in prose. The existing T-053 (replayed proof or stale authorization surviving connection change) and TB-011 do not describe a resume path. A flawed platform implementation could let a replaced or hijacked connection inherit authorization, or let a reconnect lease outlive revocation. Add a threat entry covering resumption and its deadline, revocation and nonce-binding requirements. Also add a conformance test requirement on the platform side.
findings.title: New endpoint-resumption custody response is not covered by the threat model
